title: Beyond the 956: Irma P. Hall, beloved “Soul Food” matriarch, dies at 91
excerpt: Irma P. Hall, the actress best known as Big Mama in “Soul Food” and as Marva Munson in “The Ladykillers,” died November 10, 2026, in Dallas. She was 91.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Irma P. Hall, the actress who brought warmth and authority to matriarchal roles in Soul Food and The Ladykillers, has died at 91.

Hall died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Dallas, her family announced Wednesday. No cause of death was given. The Associated Press, CNN and USA Today reported her death.

Born Irma Dolores Player on June 3, 1935, in Beaumont, Texas, Hall was raised in Chicago and later returned to Texas for college. She taught high school for 27 years before her acting career took off — at age 60, when A Family Thing brought her a major film role in 1996.

Hall was best known to many viewers as Josephine “Mother Joe” Joseph — Big Mama, the family’s steadying force — in the 1997 film Soul Food. She returned to the role in the television series based on the film.

Her career reached a new height in 2004, when she received the Cannes Film Festival Jury Prize for her performance as Marva Munson, a Bible-reading landlady opposite Tom Hanks in the Coen brothers’ comedy The Ladykillers.

Her many other credits included Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil, Beloved, Patch Adams, Collateral and Tyler Perry’s Meet the Browns, along with two Werner Herzog films. She also helped establish the Dallas Minority Repertory Theatre, and the Texas Film Hall of Fame inducted her in Austin.

Hall is survived by her daughter, Irma Hall Crayton.

Rest in Peace, Irma P. Hall.

Sources: The Associated Press; CNN; USA Today.
